question: Motion to Discharge S. Res. 852
bill_title: A resolution requesting information on Israel's human rights practices pursuant to section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.
plain_language: This was a vote to pull from committee a resolution requesting information on Israel's human rights practices under section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act. It is not a final vote on the resolution. A Yea would have brought it to the floor; a Nay leaves it in committee.

question: H. Con. Res. 89
bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
plain_language: This House resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea would agree to that direction. A Nay rejects the resolution.

question: H.R. 5334, as amended
bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
plain_language: As rewritten, this bill imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea passes that Senate version. A Nay votes against passage.

question: Paul Amdt. No. 6715
bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
plain_language: This amendment would replace sections 113 through 117 of the Russia-sanctions text with exceptions for humanitarian goods, intelligence and law-enforcement work, certain treaty obligations, civilian nuclear cooperation, and some space launches, plus rules for waiving or ending sanctions. A Yea adopts that replacement. A Nay rejects it.

question: Motion to Discharge S.J. Res. 181
bill_title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against the Islamic Republic of Iran that have not been authorized by Congress.
plain_language: This vote would pull S.J.Res. 181 out of committee so the Senate can consider it; it is not a final vote on the joint resolution. The joint resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran unless a declaration of war or authorization to use military force for such purpose has been enacted. A Yea discharges it; a Nay leaves it in committee.

question: Motion to Proceed to H.R. 5334
bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
plain_language: This vote is on whether the Senate takes up H.R. 5334 (Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026), which imposes a variety of sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions related to Russia, extends an Iran-related sanctions law, and expands a tax deduction for teacher expenses to include early childhood educators. A Yea begins consideration; a Nay blocks it for now.

question: Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Motion to Proceed to H.R. 5334
result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (86-12, 3/5 majority required)
bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
plain_language: This vote would end debate on whether to take up H.R. 5334 (Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026), which imposes a variety of sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions related to Russia, extends an Iran-related sanctions law, and expands a tax deduction for teacher expenses to include early childhood educators. Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the bill; a Nay keeps debate open.

question: Is the Point of Order Well Taken Re: To the Privilege Status of S.J. Res. 98
result: Point of Order Well Taken (50-50, Vice President of the United States, voted Yea)
bill_title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
plain_language: S.J.Res. 98 directs the President to end the use of U.S. Armed Forces for hostilities within or against Venezuela unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force. This vote was on a point of order challenging whether the resolution qualifies for the fast-track (privileged) procedure; the Vice President broke a 50-50 tie. A Yea sustains the point of order; a Nay rejects it.
